label: Pause for the Word
theme: God's herbs, nature, and the beauty of Creation
title: The Earth Declares His Glory
key_verse: Genesis 1:29 (KJV) - 'And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth...' and Bob Marley: 'Every leaf that grows tells you that God exists.'
reflection: As evening falls, look around. The herbs of the earth, the trees standing tall, the green that feeds us—these are not accidents. They are God's signature written across creation. The Quran teaches us that the heavens and the earth declare His wisdom. Every plant, every seed, every root reaching deep into soil speaks a language older than words. Bob Marley understood this truth: 'Every leaf that grows tells you that God exists.' When we pause to notice—the scent of evening air, the color fading in the sky, the quiet strength of growing things—we meet the Divine not in temples alone, but in the garden itself. Emperor Haile Selassie taught that nature is the book of God, open for all to read. This evening, let your heart be still. Let the creation speak. In its beauty, you will find peace, and in that peace, you will find Him.
closing_blessing: May the stillness of this evening bring you closer to the Creator's heart. Blessings and light unto you. Selah.

theme: wealth, the poor, and true spiritual riches
title: The Measure of True Riches
wells_drawn: Rastafari teaching (Emperor Haile Selassie I's words and groundation reasoning)
key_verse: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:261 (paraphrased) & Haile Selassie I (1963 United Nations Address)
reflection: Midday arrives with the full rush of trade, ambition, and commerce. In this pause, let us ground ourselves in what actually endures. The Holy Quran reminds us in Surah Al-Baqarah that the likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a single grain which grows seven ears, and in every ear a hundred grains. True increase does not belong to the hoarder; it belongs to the generous hand. Emperor Haile Selassie the First, speaking before the United Nations in 1963, declared that until the basic human rights are equally guaranteed to all without regard to race or status, true peace remains an illusion. Rastafari groundation reasoning teaches that worldly riches in Babylon are fleeting, but righteousness and care for the needy build a spiritual fortress that no storm can wash away. Look at the brother and sister next to you with kindness. If God has blessed your table today, extend your hand to lift someone whose cup is empty.
closing_blessing: May your work be blessed and your spirit remain untainted by greed. Selah. This stream reminds us. Ring reminders: return to the Word, with regards to the word.
label: Pause for the Word
